thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Service serving-runtime-prod is reporting repeated model warmup failures and increased 5xx on /v1/generate. Severity: P1. Auto-retries failing. Notifying on-call.

ana: getting paged. seeing a spike in model-load errors in the logs: `deser: invalid magic header` followed by `compile timeout` for a few models during warmup.

matt: when did this start? any customer-facing latency spikes yet?

ana: started ~15m ago. CPU & GPU hosts flapping briefly. Grafana shows a 12% error rate for the last 10m, tail latency up. A few big customers reporting soft-failures.

sasha: I can pull the warmup logs and the artifact integrity check. Might be an artifact roll pushed around the same time as a model update.

ana: logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z WARN warmup: deserialization failed for model redwood-q4-v1 - deser: invalid magic header
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR runtime: compile timed out after 30s for kernel selection
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR gpu: cuda error 700 (illegal memory access) while compiling
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z INFO warmup: fallback to cpu-quantized variant
2026-03-15T14:03:00Z ERROR container: pod serving-runtime-prod-45 restart backoff
```

matt: looks like two things: corrupted artifact (invalid header) and subsequent compile timeouts causing OOM/CUDA errors. Could be a bad build published to the model store.

ana: agreed. Rolling back to previous artifact on a single pool to validate. Initiating canary rollback to pool-2.

ops-bot: Runbook hint: `warmup-failure` -> step 2: verify model artifact checksum, step 4: toggle fallback model, step 7: notify customers. Link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/warmup-failure

sasha: checksum mismatch confirmed on S3 for `redwood-q4-v1/2026-03-15/weights.tar.gz`. Local checksum: `ad3f...c9` vs recorded `00ff...11`. Likely bad push.

ryan: re-deploying previous artifact to canary pool now. Command: `infractl deploy --model redwood-q4-v1 --version v20260301 --pool pool-2 --no-warmup`

ana: also increasing compile timeout to 90s temporarily for compiling jit kernels to reduce compile-time aborts: `kubectl set env ds/serving-runtime COMPILE_TIMEOUT=90s -n serving-prod`

matt: good. For GPU illegal memory access, let's cordon the node that had repeated CUDA errors (node-gpu-7). `kubectl cordon node-gpu-7` and drain non-critical pods.

ana: cordon+drain started. moving warmup jobs off node-gpu-7.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 10:18 UTC - Canary rollback started; rollback expected to finish in ~5m. Impact: 8% of requests currently seeing 5xx, top affected customer: finanalytics-inc (20% of their calls). Page routed to matt.

sasha: for immediate mitigation, we switched warmup behavior to `lazy-load` (no eager compile) for the affected pools to avoid triggering the compile path on start. `config: warmup_mode=lazy-load`

matt: that should reduce risk. Are any dedicated customers pinned to the bad artifact?

ana: two dedicated tenants had model pins to `latest`. We're patching them to `v20260301`. Sending notifications to account owners now. Draft msg: "We observed intermittent 5xx during model warmup and have rolled back your model to the previous stable artifact; no data exposure expected."

ryan: rollback to v20260301 finished on pool-2. Warmup success logs show `loaded weights, kv cache ready` and no compile timeouts for canary.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 10:24 UTC - Canary green. Error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% in canary pool. Scheduling rolling rollback to remaining production pools with 1-min ramp and monitoring.

ana: starting rolling rollback to pool-1 and pool-3 with stagger. Also enabling `auto-fallback=on` for older CPU-safe variants to reduce customer impact until all pools are stable.

matt: for postmortem, capture root cause: bad artifact published to model store. Need to add artifact checksum gating in publish pipeline and a post-publish smoke test with warmup on an isolated node.

sasha: opened ticket: INFRA-2346 - "Model publisher: add checksum verification and warmup smoke test" and assigned to infra-pipeline.

ryan: customer comms: pinged finanalytics-inc support@finanalytics with incident summary and remediation ETA. Also added SLO/incident header to status page.

ana: nodes: node-gpu-7 shows repeated `cuda error 700` once artifact started failing—likely caused by the runtime trying to compile malformed kernels. After cordon it looks stable. Will mark for deeper hardware check later.

matt: preparing to hand off. I will update the incident channel with summary and notify next on-call at 14:45 UTC. Any outstanding actions for the next shift?

ana: stuff to follow up: 1) Verify artifact publishing pipeline fix landed 2) Run full regtests on v20260301 before unpinning tenants 3) Validate node-gpu-7 hardware logs and kernel driver versions 4) Draft customer postmortem for impacted tenants.

sasha: adding those to the incident ticket INF-2290 and tagging eng-runtime and infra-pipeline.

matt: ok taking handoff. tl;dr: P1 warmup failures due to corrupted artifact -> rollback to stable version across pools, temporary compile timeout bump & lazy warmup applied, node cordoned, affected customers notified. Remaining: follow-ups in ticket, hardware check, publishing pipeline change.

incidents-bot: HANDOFF: matt -> ana (next on-call) at 14:45 UTC. Please ack.

ana: acked. will pick up monitoring & customer threads.

matt: leaving notes in the runbook under the incident entry and attaching logs + checksums. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLUTION: 11:05 UTC - Error rates returned to baseline (<=1%). Incident resolved but follow-ups open.

ana: creating short postmortem draft and will add timeline + mitigations.

sasha: recommending a minor change: make artifact pushes write to a "quarantine" bucket and auto-run warmup smoke test before promoting to active model store.

matt: agreed. will prioritize INFRA-2346 in next sprint.

ryan: thanks team. I'll update status page and send a short customer note to impacted accounts with link to postmortem when ready.

ana: closing thread for live mitigation. Will leave follow-ups in tickets.
